title: Minimax Rates for Regression Discontinuity with a Noisy Score and Test-Retest Calibration
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal:below-floor; matched minimax and honest-interval frontier unproved after five D0 solve rounds
gap_reasons: The core replaces the promised matched minimax risk/shortest-interval frontier and attaining rate with a lower rate plus an unresolved profile-diameter bracket; the current derivation is therefore below the proposed frontier claim.

The sieve proof wrongly treats a bounded C^r ball (integer beta in the stated range) as closed/compact under uniform convergence: smooth functions with uniformly bounded C^1 norms can converge uniformly to a non-C^1 Lipschitz function, so nonempty relaxed Lambda_j need not yield a legal limit in M_beta and the implemented endpoints are not proved equal to the displayed profile extrema; replace this step with a topology/closure argument valid at integral beta (and re-establish endpoint equality and the diameter upper bounds).
proof_attempt_summary: Five D0 solve rounds established identification, the Bernoulli reduction, joint affinity, moment compensation, and legal same-class endpoint witnesses for the declared Hölder range. They yielded point-risk and honest-length lower bounds of order min{eta_beta(n),m^-1/2}, but did not prove the matching cross-scale upper rate, the fixed-scale rho_w converse, or an attaining interval. The integer-beta compactness objection also leaves the proposed profile estimator and exact upper bracket unproved.
tldr: Threshold assignment uses a noisy score whose Gaussian scale is informed jointly by the main-score tails and independent test--retest differences. For every fixed \(\beta\in[1/2,\bar\beta]\) in the declared range, a legal positive-Hölder inverse-heat pair proves the same-class lower rate \(\min\{\eta_\beta(n),m^{-1/2}\}\) for point risk and honest expected length, with lower-bound calibration elbow \(m\asymp k_n^{4\beta+8}\). The explicit finite-sample profile midpoint and projected interval retain valid upper guarantees, but no matching expected-diameter rate is proved; the \(\rho_w\) lower component and additive matched frontier remain open. The result remains an achieved subfield-tier converse and finite-sample inference result, below the field-tier matched-frontier objective.
gap: Known-noise noisy-score RD fixes the convolution operator; known-error linear-functional deconvolution does the same; repeated-measurement deconvolution studies density or regression recovery in different observation schemes. None gives the joint rate for a fixed causal latent contrast when the Gaussian scale is learned from both main-score tails and a separate calibration sample.
fill: A legal inverse-heat moment construction and a matching endpoint-polynomial score are combined with one-sided optimal recovery, exact two-sample affinity, and bias-aware inversion over the full-law class to deliver the estimator, an explicit Bernoulli same-class lower bound, shortest honest interval length, and both calibration transition boundaries.
